Lessons.Title: Multiplication and Division PLC Activity
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will use a variety of representations to illustrate the relationship between multiplication and division to develop fluency with division within 100.
In previous units, you learned the meaning of multiplication and division and understood division as an unknown-factor problem. You have worked to develop fluency with multiplication within 100. In this lesson, you continue that work by reinforcing your understanding of the relationship between multiplication and division.

Warm-up Which One Doesn't Belong: Multiplication and Division. Four original pictures A–D need teacher visual review; plausible labels alone do not determine which one is different, and more than one justified choice may be correct.

Activity 1 Card Sort: Find the Match (25 minutes). Each learner receives an equation or diagram card and finds a peer with an equivalent situation or quantity. Partners create a poster with the cards, an additional different diagram, and a related real-world division situation, explaining the multiplication–division relationship.

Activity 2 Find the Match Gallery Walk (10 minutes). Pairs examine others' posters, describe a representation unlike their own, and explain a relationship between multiplication and division on another poster.
Independent example, not a publisher card: 6 equal groups of 4 contain 24 objects; 6 × 4 = 24, 24 ÷ 6 = 4, and 24 ÷ 4 = 6. The two divisions ask different questions.

The original visual cards and warm-up A–D images have not been pixel-verified; original publisher Cool-down is gated. Teacher evaluates diagrams, partner matches, classroom presentations and reasoning.
Source-authentic activity scripts are teacher mediated. Figures, print-only masters and publisher-gated Cool-downs not independently inspected are not claimed source-identical.

KeyConcepts.Title: Preserved valid source-bound concepts
KeyConcepts.Definition:
Key ideas:
- Interpret representations of the relationship between multiplication and division
- Represent the relationship between multiplication and division
- Multiplication can represent equal groups, arrays, rates, or scaling; each factor must have a clear meaning in the context.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use in conjunction with the individually verified 2021 activity directions.
KeyConcepts.Example: Learning goal: You will use a variety of representations to illustrate the relationship between multiplication and division to develop fluency with division within 100.

KeyConcepts.Title: Inverse operations
KeyConcepts.Definition: Multiplication and division can describe the same equal-group quantities.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Keep group count, group size and total consistent.

KeyConcepts.Title: Representations
KeyConcepts.Definition: An equation, diagram or story can refer to one equal-group situation.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check the same total and group relationships, not superficial appearance.

KeyConcepts.Title: Gallery explanation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Recognize and explain another learner's valid equivalent representation.
KeyConcepts.Example: Explain a partition and corresponding product.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent matched-card reasoning
WorkedExamples.Question: Create a diagram and equations for 24 items placed into 6 equal groups.
Steps: Draw six groups containing four items.
Write 24 ÷ 6 = 4 and explain one group size.
Write 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and explain the number of groups.
WorkedExamples.Check: Explain the mathematical relationship, and keep independently authored examples distinct from source worksheets.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Matching cards only because they show the same digits.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Equivalent groups require identical quantities and relationships.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Confusing number of groups with items per group.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Name both the number of groups and the group size.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Inferring specific quantities from uninspected A–D artwork.
